title: Car Paint Materials
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement an automotive PBR material showcase scene, with a procedurally modeled sedan and support for real-time adjustment of paint color and material parameters. Refer to the official three.js example webgl_materials_car, but modify it substantially (fully procedural modeling, with no external models).

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Procedural Car Model]
The model must be created entirely procedurally (do not load any external GLB/OBJ files), using a combination of basic geometries:

(1) Body base: BoxGeometry(4, 0.8, 2), positioned at y=0.6; this is the lower portion of the main car body.
(2) Body top: BoxGeometry(2.5, 0.7, 1.8), positioned at y=1.35 (passenger compartment/cabin section), offset rearward to x=-0.3.
(3) Hood: BoxGeometry(1.2, 0.15, 1.8), positioned at y=1.0, x=1.2 (front section, inclined). A ShearMatrix or vertex adjustment may be used to create a slight incline.
(4) Trunk: BoxGeometry(0.8, 0.15, 1.8), positioned at y=1.0, x=-1.8.
(5) Windshield: PlaneGeometry(1.8, 0.8), inclined by approximately 30°, with a translucent glass material (MeshPhysicalMaterial, transmission=0.8, roughness=0.05, ior=1.5).
(6) Rear windshield: Same as above, but positioned at the rear.
(7) Four wheels (4 total): Each wheel uses CylinderGeometry(radius=0.35, width=0.2), rotated 90° along the Z axis. Positions:
  - Front left: (1.2, 0.35, 1.1)
  - Front right: (1.2, 0.35, -1.1)
  - Rear left: (-1.2, 0.35, 1.1)
  - Rear right: (-1.2, 0.35, -1.1)
  Wheel material: dark gray rubber (roughness=0.9, metalness=0.0, color=#333333).
(8) Chrome trim: 2 elongated BoxGeometry objects along both sides of the car body, using MeshStandardMaterial(metalness=1.0, roughness=0.05, color=#cccccc).
(9) Front and rear bumpers: BoxGeometry slightly wider than the car body, with a dark material.

The body material (shared by body, hood, trunk, and top): MeshPhysicalMaterial, with parameters controlled by the UI.

[Paint Color]
(10) id="paintColor": Contains 8 color buttons/options. Preset colors:
  - "#cc0000" (bright red), "#003366" (dark blue), "#ffffff" (pearl white), "#1a1a1a" (obsidian black),
  - "#8b7355" (champagne gold), "#2e8b57" (British racing green), "#708090" (cement gray), "#800020" (burgundy red)
(11) "#cc0000" (bright red) is selected by default.

[Material Parameters]
(12) id="clearcoat": range slider, min=0, max=1, step=0.01, default 1.0. Controls MeshPhysicalMaterial.clearcoat.
(13) id="metalness": range slider, min=0, max=1, step=0.01, default 0.9. Controls MeshPhysicalMaterial.metalness.
(14) id="roughness": range slider, min=0, max=1, step=0.01, default 0.1. Controls MeshPhysicalMaterial.roughness.
(15) Immediately update the car body material properties whenever a slider changes (the changes must be reflected in the rendering in real time).

[Ground and Environment]
(16) Ground plane: large PlaneGeometry(50, 50), at y=0, using MeshPhysicalMaterial(color=#555555, metalness=0.0, roughness=0.8, clearcoat=0.3), simulating showroom floor reflections.
(17) Use PMREMGenerator to generate a simple environment map from a color gradient (or DataTexture noise), and apply it to the scene.

[Camera and Lighting]
(18) Use OrbitControls with autoRotate enabled (slowly rotating showcase). Initial position (6, 3, 6), looking toward the center of the car.
(19) White DirectionalLight from (5, 10, 5), with intensity 1.5.
(20) HemisphereLight(skyColor=#ffffff, groundColor=#444444, intensity=0.6).

[State Exposure (Required; Update Every Frame or After Each Operation)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  paintColor: string,         // Current paint color, such as "#cc0000"
  clearcoat: number,          // Clearcoat value, 0-1
  metalness: number,          // Metalness, 0-1
  roughness: number,          // Roughness, 0-1
  wheelCount: number,         // Number of wheels (should be 4)
  bodyPartCount: number       // Number of body parts (body base, top, hood, trunk, windshields, bumpers, etc.; should be > 5)
}

Output a single standalone HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
